definition: A neural architecture based on self-attention rather than recurrence or convolution, the foundation of modern LLMs.
details: The Transformer processes entire sequences in parallel, using multi-head self-attention to model pairwise relationships and positional encodings to retain order. Removing recurrence made training dramatically more parallelizable, enabling the scaling that produced GPT, BERT and today’s large language models.

explainer.lead: The Transformer is the design inside almost every modern language model. Instead of reading a sentence one word at a time, it looks at every word at once and lets each word decide which others matter to it.
explainer.eli5: A transformer reads a whole sentence at once and lets every word look at every other word to work out what it means, then stacks that step many times to build up understanding.
explainer.practitioner: A stack of identical blocks, each a multi-head self-attention layer followed by a feed-forward MLP, with residual connections and layer normalization around both. Tokens get embeddings plus positional information (sinusoidal, learned, or rotary). Decoder-only stacks (GPT, Llama) use causal masking for generation; encoder-only stacks (BERT) suit classification and embeddings; encoder–decoder (T5) suits translation and summarisation.
explainer.paperLevel: Vaswani et al. (2017) replaced recurrence with scaled dot-product attention, softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V, in h parallel heads, interleaved with position-wise feed-forward networks, residual paths and layer normalization. The base model used d_model = 512, 8 heads and 6 encoder plus 6 decoder layers. Because every position attends to every other in one step, the maximum path length between tokens is O(1) and training parallelises across the sequence, at O(n²·d) cost per layer.
explainer.example: Given the prompt "The capital of France is", a decoder-only transformer attends over all five tokens in each layer and its final layer assigns high probability to "Paris" as the next token.

components.name: Token embeddings
components.detail: turn each word piece into a vector of numbers

components.name: Positional encoding
components.detail: adds each token's position, since attention alone ignores order

components.name: Multi-head self-attention
components.detail: every token weighs every other token, several ways in parallel

components.name: Feed-forward layer
components.detail: a small network applied to each token on its own

components.name: Residual connections + layer norm
components.detail: keep signals stable across dozens of stacked blocks

components.name: Output head
components.detail: turns the final vectors into probabilities for the next token

flow: Text is split into tokens and each token becomes an embedding.
Position information is added so the model knows word order.
A feed-forward layer refines each token's vector.
The attention + feed-forward block repeats N times.
The last layer predicts the next token (or a label).
explainer.origin: Introduced in 2017 by Ashish Vaswani and colleagues at Google in the paper “Attention Is All You Need”, originally for machine translation.
explainer.lineage: It replaced recurrent networks such as LSTMs for most language tasks, and led directly to BERT, GPT and today's large language models.
explainer.whyItMatters: Because it processes a whole sequence in parallel, it trains far faster on modern hardware — which is what made scaling to billions of parameters practical.
